title: One Tanker's Worth, Borrowed

source.title: Energy Dept to loan part of home heating oil reserve to ease prices, drawing bipartisan praise
source.note: published 10-21 14:58 ET. Fox's station on the roster is 'RI?' — proposed, ruling owed; scored as RI on the 10-20 precedent (fox_2026-10-20_hormuz_mines), the Diesel Index's RI seat, flag on the figure. Read in full via fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over fifteen words

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c — 'diesel prices will come down')

zAxis.pos: prices come down by the deal
zAxis.neg: they do not — relief is sourced elsewhere, or not at all

transformNote: the promise of 10-09/10-11: Russian diesel 'immediately', and prices 'will be coming down'. Twelve days on, the executive reaches for a reserve: 315,000 barrels of distillate loaned from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, landing by 11-13, to be returned with a premium before the 2027-28 season. The cut does the arithmetic the page does not: 315,000 bbl of distillate ≈ 42,000 t — one Russian tanker's worth (the first cargo, 40,000 t, sailed 10-22), borrowed from next winter. The relief the page records is not the deal's; the page never mentions the deal

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: Energy Dept to loan part of home heating oil reserve to ease prices, drawing bipartisan praise
lines.note: THE DOOR: 'ease' and 'bipartisan praise' — the frame is consensus; the headline withholds the size (a third of the reserve) and the cause (the war). 'Loan' is the honest word and it is in the headline
lines.zWhy: a reserve loaned to ease prices concedes the deal has not

lines.quote: DOE plans to loan up to about one-third of the emergency heating oil reserve to ease price pressures as global conflicts constrain supply
lines.note: sized as a fraction; the cause is 'global conflicts' — unnamed, plural. The deal that was to be the remedy is absent
lines.zWhy: a third of the emergency reserve going out twelve days after the deal is relief sourced elsewhere

lines.quote: up to 315,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, which holds one million barrels of ultra-low sulfur distillate at four sites
lines.note: THE SIZE: 315,000 bbl of distillate ≈ 42,000 t — one Russian tanker's worth (the first cargo, 40,000 t, sailed 10-22). The arithmetic is the cut's; the page sets the number beside nothing
lines.zWhy: one cargo's worth from a domestic reserve, where the schedule said 300,000 t from Russia

lines.quote: borrowers must return the same volume plus a premium before the 2027-28 heating season
lines.note: a loan, not a sale: the barrels come back with interest. The relief is borrowed from next winter
lines.zWhy: relief that must be repaid with a premium is not a price coming down

lines.quote: committed to doing everything in our power to lower energy costs; the exchange directed after receiving Senators Collins' and King's letter
lines.note: constitutive — the act's holder. The cause he names for the act is the letter, not the deal; the deal is not in his statement

lines.quote: a temporary measure to solve a temporary supply disruption; build the Constitution Pipeline and replace home heating oil with natural gas
lines.note: the holder's own clock ('temporary', twice) and his real answer — a pipeline years out. The remedy he names is not the one the principal named on 10-11

lines.quote: approximately half of Maine households rely on fuel oil; the release should put downward pressure on home heating oil costs
lines.note: a senator whose seat is on the slate (me-sen) credits a federal act thirteen days before the election. 'Should' is the tense; the pressure is anticipated
lines.zWhy: a release that 'should' put downward pressure is relief hoped for, not read

lines.quote: a 13% increase in New England home heating oil supplies; heating oil costs have risen 70% from a year ago
lines.note: THE PRICE: +70% year on year, twelve days after the deal; 13% of supply against 70% of price. The lowest-Dia line on the page
lines.zWhy: seventy percent up is the price not coming down

lines.quote: Maine has been hit especially hard by the run-up in fuel prices since the beginning of the Iran War
lines.note: THE CAUSE NAMED: the war, by the independent — not Ukraine's refinery strikes (the principal's cause of 10-15, msnow_2026-10-15). The arc's cause stated in the RI corner
lines.zWhy: a run-up dated to the war's start is a price the deal has not touched

lines.quote: the cost is absolutely through the roof; the release should provide some help
lines.note: 'through the roof' is the page's one verdict word; 'some help' is the measure of the act in the senator's own mouth
lines.zWhy: 'some help' against 'through the roof' is relief smaller than the gap

lines.quote: releases to be completed by Nov. 13 from Boston, South Portland and New Haven
lines.note: THE CLOCK: the barrels land ten days after the election (11-03). The act is announced before the vote and delivered after it
lines.zWhy: relief dated after the election is not relief before it

lines.quote: no more than 150,000 barrels per site; 25,000-barrel minimum offer; competitive among retailers and terminal holders
lines.note: the mechanics — the only line on the page that is pure instrument
dated: the act becomes barrels on 10-27 at the earliest, a week before the vote
lines.zWhy: a bid date a week out is relief still on paper
